content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [product_name] 24v basic unit [article_no] FS02 from 2015. I want to use Modbus, so I need a new basic unit with at least FS04. However, I also have a [product_name] expansion module [article_no] FS02 from 2015. Do I need to replace this expansion module for Modbus to work fully, or is it sufficient to just replace the basic (main) unit?
All expansion modules with order numbers ending in [article_no] are compatible with every [product_name] base module-related hardware.
Thanks for confirming. The new basic (main) module is [article_no]. Is my older expansion module [article_no] FS02 from 2015 also compatible and accessible from the new main module [article_no]?

The current [product_name] [article_no] is a [version_no] model of the 4th generation, and is referred to as [product_name] [version_no]. In programming, you need to select [product_name] [version_no] under hardware selection. All models since September 2014 are [version_no].

Thanks for clarifying. I understand the current [article_no] is a [product_name] 4th generation model and should be programmed by choosing [product_name] [version_no]. My question is, will my older DM16R expansion module from 2015 ([article_no] FS02) work with the new and current [article_no]? Is it fully compatible and will it function properly when using Modbus?
Your expansion module will work with the current [product_name] [version_no] release. However, the expansion module itself isn't directly related to Modbus operation.

I was asking because I want to access I/O from my expansion module through Modbus, since the Modbus feature requires a newer main module. I thought a new expansion module was necessary too. Now I see that I can keep my existing expansion module. Thank you for the clarification.

Modbus communicates with the base module, not directly with expansion modules. The expansion module exchanges data with the base module. So, a Modbus device accesses the status of digital inputs via the base module.

Yes, access is via the base module. What confused me is that Modbus support was introduced for the [product_name] as of FS04, and my expansion module is FS02, so I wasn't sure about compatibility. Do expansion modules also have hardware versions like FS03, FS04, etc., or just the base modules?

The FS versions of base modules and extension modules are separate and can't be directly compared. FS status refers to each hardware series individually. To repeat, all expansion modules with order numbers ending in [article_no] are compatible with all [product_name] basic modules, regardless of FS version.

analysis.insight_summary: Community members explored whether upgrading to a newer [product_name] base module for Modbus support required replacing the expansion module as well. Experienced users clarified that as long as the expansion module is identified by a specific [article_no], it remains compatible with all relevant base modules, regardless of hardware version. Modbus functionality is accessed via the base module, not directly through expansion modules.
analysis.user_expectations: User anticipates that existing expansion modules will work seamlessly with the upgraded [product_name] base module for Modbus applications, without needing to replace the expansion units.
